findings.title: Accidental git submodule committed
findings.body: This adds a gitlink named sentry-repo pointing at a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a (the PR base) and does not add a .gitmodules entry. Merging records a broken submodule in the tree that is unrelated to error upsampling. Checkouts and tools that resolve gitlinks will fail or pull an unintended nested repository.

findings.title: Substring check treats negated and mixed queries as error-only
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query returns true whenever the raw query string contains "event.type:error". That matches "!event.type:error" and "event.type:error OR event.type:transaction", so those discover queries are treated as error-focused. After every project is allowlisted, count() is rewritten to sum(sample_weight). Transactions do not have that column (or have it null), so a normal negated or mixed stats query either fails in Snuba or returns a wrong count instead of the raw count. The docstring says the check errs on the side of caution; a substring test does the opposite.

findings.title: Upsampling uses the outer dataset and request query, not the query being run
findings.body: _get_event_stats decides upsampling from the closed-over dataset and request.GET, ignoring scoped_dataset and the query argument it is about to execute. The dashboard-widget splitter calls this with rewritten queries such as "({query}) AND event.type:transaction" and "({query}) AND !event.type:transaction", and sometimes with the discover dataset while the outer dataset is a metrics dataset. A transaction probe therefore still rewrites count() to sum(sample_weight) whenever the original request looked like an error query, so check_if_results_have_data can see empty weights and save_split_decision persists the wrong discover split. The error-only probe does the reverse: it will not upsample unless the original query string already contained event.type:error, so split error widgets keep raw counts.

findings.title: Eligibility cache key uses process-randomized hash()
findings.body: The cache key is built with Python's builtin hash() of the project-id tuple. hash() is salted by PYTHONHASHSEED, so the same organization and projects produce different keys in different workers. The shared cache therefore does not reuse another worker's result, and invalidate_upsampling_cache deletes a key no other process wrote. Allowlist changes cannot be flushed, and the 60-second cache does not actually avoid repeated option lookups across the fleet. Build the key from a stable digest of the sorted project ids. This also adds a remote cache round-trip to every events-stats request, including spans and transactions that can never upsample.

findings.title: Integration tests share a 60s cache and bypass the options mock
findings.body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects caches allowlist eligibility for 60 seconds using only organization id and project ids. These tests reuse the same two projects and only change the mocked options.get return value, but a cache hit never calls options.get. After test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects stores True, the partial-allowlist and empty-allowlist tests still upsample and assert count == 1, so they fail whenever the test cache retains values (Django locmem does). setUp does not clear the cache, and the unit tests never call the cached function, so this path is untested and order-dependent.

findings.title: sum(sample_weight) zeroes legacy events and truncates fractional weights
findings.body: upsampled_count is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no coalesce. ClickHouse sum skips nulls, so events stored before sample_weight was set contribute nothing: once a project is allowlisted, historical error buckets become 0 instead of the real count. toInt64 also truncates toward zero, so one event with weight 1/0.3 (about 3.33) is reported as 3, and a float sum of 9.999 becomes 9. Counts are silently low. Aggregate round(sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))) so missing weights still count as 1.

findings.title: Factory writes sample_rate, query sums sample_weight
findings.body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling copies contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate onto sample_rate (0.1 in the new stats tests). Nothing in this change sets sample_weight or stores the multiplier 1/client_sample_rate. The new aggregate sums sample_weight, and OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest expects one stored event to count as 10. Summing a rate of 0.1 becomes 0 after toInt64, and a missing sample_weight column fails the query, so the test setup cannot produce the asserted result unless an unshown ingest step inverts sample_rate into sample_weight. The helper also runs for every store_event and overwrites an existing sample_rate whenever that context is present.
